findings.title: `queue.Queue.shutdown()` requires Python 3.13+ and will raise `AttributeError` on Python 3.11/3.12
findings.body: `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` calls `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` (line 238) and `OrderedQueueWorker.run` catches `queue.ShutDown` (lines 132 and 142). `queue.Queue.shutdown` and `queue.ShutDown` were added in Python 3.13. On earlier Python versions (such as 3.11 or 3.12), `q.shutdown` raises `AttributeError`, which is caught and logged, leaving workers blocked indefinitely on `self.work_queue.get()` (line 131) when the queue is empty and causing `OrderedQueueWorker.run` to fail with `AttributeError: module 'queue' has no attribute 'ShutDown'` whenever an exception occurs or `get()` unblocks.

findings.title: `FixedQueuePool` is shared across partition rebalances and permanently killed on strategy `close()`
findings.body: `ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__` creates a single `self.queue_pool = FixedQueuePool(...)` instance (lines 133-137) and passes it to every `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` created in `create_with_partitions` (line 255). When Arroyo rebalances partitions, it calls `close()` and `join()` (or `terminate()`) on the current strategy before calling `create_with_partitions` for the new assignment. Because `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` and `terminate()` call `self.queue_pool.shutdown()` (lines 338, 342 of `queue_consumer.py`), the shared `FixedQueuePool`'s worker threads are stopped and its queues are shut down on the first rebalance. Furthermore, its `OffsetTracker` retains stale partition/offset state across rebalances. Any subsequent strategy created by the factory will submit messages to dead queues/workers. The pool lifecycle should either be tied to each `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` instance (created in `create_with_partitions`) or `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` must not shut down a factory-owned pool without recreating it and resetting offset state.

findings.title: Calling `commit_function` from a background thread violates Arroyo's single-threaded consumer contract
findings.body: `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` spawns a background thread (`self.commit_thread`, line 270) that calls `self.commit_function(committable)` (line 287). In Arroyo, the `commit` callback passed to `create_with_partitions` calls into the underlying `KafkaConsumer.commit` / `StreamProcessor` state, which is not thread-safe and is designed to be invoked only from the processor's main polling thread (i.e., during `poll()`, `submit()`, `close()`, or `join()`). Calling `commit_function` directly from `poll()` (and once more in `close()`/`join()` after workers drain) avoids concurrent access to the Kafka consumer and eliminates the need for a separate commit thread.

findings.title: Unbounded `queue.Queue()` provides no backpressure and can exhaust memory
findings.body: `FixedQueuePool.__init__` initializes each `work_queue` with `queue.Queue()` with no `maxsize` (line 185), and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` never raises `MessageRejected` or blocks. Despite the class docstring claiming 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up' (line 253), the main Arroyo loop will read from Kafka at full speed and buffer an unbounded number of decoded payloads and `Message` objects in memory if any worker falls behind, which will also prevent offsets on that partition from advancing and cause `OffsetTracker.all_offsets` to grow without bound.

findings.title: `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()` and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` drop queued items and skip final offset commit
findings.body: In `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()` (lines 233-234), `worker.shutdown = True` is set on every worker before draining the queues. Because `OrderedQueueWorker.run()` checks `while not self.shutdown:` on each iteration (line 129), a worker will exit after finishing its current item and leave all remaining queued items unprocessed. In addition, `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` stops `commit_thread` (lines 336-337) *before* shutting down `queue_pool` (line 338), so any offsets completed while workers finish during shutdown are never committed to Kafka.

findings.title: `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` asserts the opposite of its docstring and only passes due to commit timing
findings.body: `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` states that 'errors in processing don't block offset commits for other messages' (line 1876), and `OrderedQueueWorker` indeed calls `complete_offset` in its `finally` block even when `result_processor` raises. However, the test only waits ~0.2s after processing completes—before the 1.0s `_commit_loop` timer fires—and then asserts `assert len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets` (line 1922). If the commit loop happens to run in time, this test will fail; as written it is testing that no commit happened within 200ms rather than verifying that offset 102 is committed despite the exception at offset 100.
